itinerary: Day 1-2: Arrive Islamabad, fly to Skardu
Day 3: Skardu acclimatization day and city tour
Day 4: Drive to Hushe village, final settlement
Day 5: Trek to Saicho (4-5h) along Hushe River
Day 6: Trek to Dalchangpa (4-6h), Masherbrum views
Day 7: Trek to base camp (5-6h) via Gondogoro Glacier
Day 8: Rest day at base camp (4535m)
Day 9-10: Descend to Saicho then to Hushe
Day 11: Drive back to Skardu
Day 12-13: Fly to Islamabad, international departure
pros: Clear tiered pricing: foreign USD and Pakistani PKR rates both published
Dedicated Skardu acclimatization day (Day 3) plus a base-camp rest day (Day 8)
Includes satellite phone and first-aid kit in the package
States group cap of 12 and that no technical climbing experience is required
Accommodation specified (4-5 star hotels / dome tents) and all domestic flights included
cons: Strict 14kg porter baggage limit, the lowest of the operators here
Solo price is steep at $2,200, dropping sharply only with larger groups
BC at 4535m but max point 4900m; acclimatization beyond Skardu is thin
Exclusions list typos ('Force Majuro') suggest loosely maintained page
verdict: Best for groups of 4+ who want a fully-supported, fixed 13-day package with transparent foreign and local pricing; less economical for solo trekkers.
excludes: Excludes international flights, visa fees, personal insurance, personal/technical gear (boots, ice axe, crampons), tips, and force-majeure costs.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad, airport pickup and hotel
Day 2: Scenic flight to Skardu / Karakoram
Day 3: Rest day Skardu, acclimatization hike to Kharpocho fort
Day 4: Jeep drive to Hushe village (5-7h)
Day 5: Trek to Saicho (4-5h) to pastureland
Day 6: Trek to Dalchangpa (4-6h), slightly steep terrain
Day 7: Trek to Khuspang / base camp (5-6h) on Gondogoro Glacier
Day 8: Rest day at Khuspang, photography and excursions
Day 9-10: Return via Saicho (6-8h) then Hushe (4-6h)
Day 11: Drive back to Skardu
Day 12: Flight or drive to Islamabad
pros: Acclimatization hike to Kharpocho fort on the Skardu rest day
Built-in base-camp rest day (Day 8) for photography and excursions
Four-tier group pricing published from solo down to 9-20 persons
Day 2 flight noted with views; clear 12-day structure
cons: Base camp labelled Khuspang at 4600m (max ~4600m), differs from the standard 4535m BC
Highest solo price of the set at $2,500
Group rates compress slowly ($1,500 down to only $1,300 at 9-20 people)
verdict: Best for small groups wanting a guided 12-day trek with a Skardu acclimatization hike; solo travellers pay a premium.
excludes: Excludes international flights, personal clothing, and tips to guides, cooks and porters.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad, transfer to hotel
Day 2: Early flight to Skardu, or drive to Skardu
Day 3: Jeep from Skardu to Hushe village
Day 4: Packing and preparation day
Day 5: Begin trek to Saicho, camp at Saicho
Day 6: Trek from Saicho to Dalzampa campsite
Day 7: Reach Laila Peak base camp, set up camp
Day 8: Return to Saicho
Day 9: Saicho to Hushe valley
Day 10: Return to Skardu; fly/drive to Islamabad
pros: Dedicated Day 4 packing/preparation day in Hushe before trekking
Generous porter allowance: 75kg up, 50kg down per member
Max altitude clearly stated at 4,535m base camp
Transparent about helicopter rescue fee ($25,000) being a member cost
cons: No pricing published, listed as 'TBH' / to be discussed
No group-size or solo-vs-group pricing tiers given
Compact 10-day plan with only one base-camp night, no BC rest day
No Skardu acclimatization day; goes Skardu to Hushe directly
verdict: Best for trekkers who want a shorter, leaner 10-day itinerary and will negotiate price directly; not ideal if you need upfront, comparable pricing.
excludes: Excludes international flights, personal/high-altitude gear, insurance, helicopter rescue fees ($25,000), and unforeseen expenses.

itinerary: Day 1-4: Islamabad arrival, drive via Chilas (480km) to Skardu (2300m), prep day
Day 5: Drive to Hushe valley (5-7h) via Siachen Road, lunch at Khaplu
Day 6: Trek to Saicho (3330m, 4-5h), Masherbrum views
Day 7: Trek to Laila base camp (4535m, 5-6h)
Day 8: Rest day at base camp
Day 9-11: Return trek via Saicho, Machulo, Skardu
Day 12-14: Flight/drive to Islamabad, departure
pros: Longer 12-14 day plan with an overland Chilas leg aiding gradual altitude gain
Generous porter allowance: 75kg up, 50kg down per person
Scenic-route detail (Siachen Road, Khaplu lunch) shows local route knowledge
cons: Inconsistent altitude figures on page (BC given as '4000-4500m', '4,535m', peak '6096m')
No pricing published at all, no solo-vs-group or local-vs-foreign tiers
No explicit Skardu acclimatization day before pushing to Hushe
High-altitude porters above base camp not included
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting a longer, scenic overland approach with strong porter support; weak on published pricing and clarity of altitudes.
excludes: Excludes international airfare, high-altitude porters above BC, helicopter rescue fees, personal gear, high-altitude food, and member insurance.
